ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left is an ordinary clock face, with the numbers arranged according to the clock face; on the right is a dark disk placed on the clock face, with two holes on the disk. In the figure, the two holes are located approximately at the 1 o'clock and 5 o'clock positions, and the currently visible numbers are 1 and 5. Reasoning: When the disk rotates, the relative interval between the two holes remains unchanged. If the hole that originally showed 1 rotates to show 10, then the whole is equivalent to moving from 1 to 10, and the other hole also moves in the same way, so the hole that originally showed 5 will move to 2. If the hole that originally showed 5 rotates to show 10, then the other hole that originally showed 1 moves in the same way and will arrive at 6. Therefore the number that the other hole may show is 2 or 6.

method.method_draft: Read the image first: the two holes on the dark disc are shown at about the 1 o’clock and 5 o’clock positions, and in the unrotated picture they reveal 1 and 5 on the watch face. Read the text: the disc is rotated until 10 appears through one hole. Because rotating the disc keeps the spacing between the holes unchanged, move both visible positions by the same amount. If the hole that used to show 1 is now on 10, that is a shift of 3 clock numbers, so the other hole moves from 5 to 2. If instead the hole that used to show 5 is the one on 10, the other hole moves from 1 to 6. So the other hole could show 2 or 6.
